Headache is an annoying pain that can keep you from focusing and doing any work. More importantly it seems like such meaningless and senseless pain but every type of headaches have a cause or reason and can be appropriately treated once you figure out what the cause of your headache are.

Migraine is one such painful headache. 80% of people in a study conducted in 2004 showed that people who were diagnosed with sinus headaches, had no signs of actual sinuses but in fact had migraines.

Types of Headaches

Tension Headaches

With the amount of things to get done, deadlines to meet, and stuff that goes wrong in between in our daily lives it is hard not to feel stressed out or tensed. A lot of people get headache before a job interview, public speaking, or big presentation or anticipating an exam or conversation – this can cause some rather acute headaches which are painful and more than a little disorienting and distracting.

Cluster Headaches

These headaches occur more in men but aren’t completely absent in women. These headaches occur in clusters of circles in the corner of the head and can be rather crippling in the moment that they are happening. The cause for these type of headaches are still unknown, which is why doctors suspect that it is mainly genetics and hereditary traits that cause these kinds of headaches. But these can be made less recurring with certain medication.

Sinus Headaches

These headaches are rather obvious and are caused when the sinus gets inflamed, usually due to an infection. The sinus itself, as well as the headache can be treated with the appropriately prescribed medication.

Migraine Headache

Migraines are the worst of these headaches since they are the most painful and hardest to treat. A migraine headache can last anywhere between four to seventy-two hours and sometimes medication can refuse to work on your body in order to relieve you from the pain. Nausea, vision distortion and hyper sensitivity to light and sound are an associate with such types of headaches. A migraine headache is usually one sided and the pain is persistent and interrupts your day.

Combating Headache

There are a number of ways to combat headache. There are many types of medication out there to help in this area but there are also a number of home remedies and one may try them out.

  • Drinking a lot of water is always helpful. Many times, if you notice that you get headaches more frequently in the summer, it is because of dehydration.
  • Placing an ice pack on your head will help shrink the blood vessels and numb the pain till it is alleviated completely.
  • For some people, hot water bags on the neck helps release the tension and stop the throbbing head pain.
  • Lemons and apples not only help in balancing in the acid-alkaline levels in the body but may also reduce the headache as well.
